newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh braces as severe storm nears.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh braces as severe storm nears.

text.p: A severe storm brewing in the Bay of Bengal may hit Bangladesh early on Tuesday, weather officials said on Monday.
They said the country had already begun to feel the storm's effects, as heavy rain and wind speeds of 35 kph were reported.
Government officials said a tidal surge up to three feet (one meter) high swept through the southern coastal towns of Cox's Bazar and Bhola.
"The storm is about 480 km (288 miles) away from here and may hit the coastal areas around 3 a.m. on Tuesday," said one weather official in Cox's Bazar.
Officials with the Cyclone Preparedness Centre in the southern port city of Chittagong said the sea had turned rough.
"High waves slamming the coast breached flood-protection embankments at several points," an official at the centre said.
Centre officials said low-lying areas of Maheshkhali, Kutibdia, Ramgati and Hatia had already been inundated and evacuation of residents from those areas had begun.
Weather officials said all ships were advised to stay in port. The bad weather has forced the loading and unloading of cargo at the southern port of Mongla to be suspended, port officials said.
